definition: Techniques to constrain token selection during generation.
details: Techniques to constrain token selection during generation.

explainer.lead: Top-k and top-p sampling constrain which tokens a model may pick during generation. They matter because they are the main knobs for trading off randomness against coherence in output.

tiers.eli5: Instead of letting the model pick any next word, you give it a shortlist and let it choose from that. Top-k fixes the list size; top-p fixes how much probability the list must cover.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tune these per task, tighter for factual answers and looser for creative writing. A pitfall is settings too loose, which lets unlikely tokens through and derails the text.
tiers.paperLevel: Both restrict the sampling distribution at each step. Top-k keeps the k most probable tokens; top-p keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability exceeds p.

explainer.example: With top-k set to 50, the model samples only among its 50 most likely next tokens at each step.
